This writ petition has been filed, challenging the impugned order of the 1sdt respondent dated 28.02.2024 and the consequent removal order of the 2 nd respondent dated 01.03.2024 and consequently directing the respondents to reinstate the petitioner as a Non- Judicial Member for the remaining term with all incumbent emoluments and benefits accruing.

2.The case of the petitioner is that he was appointed as a Non-Judicial Member in the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Chennai, vide G.O Ms.No. 29 Cooperation, Food and Consumer Protection Department, Chennai dated 15.03.2022 and he assumed charge on 18.03.2022.

sentences.text: Whileso, on the basis of a complaint made by the Personal Assistant to the Hon'ble Judge of this Court, a criminal case was registered against the petitioner in Crime No.8 of 2023 for offences punishable under Sections 417, 419, 511 & 420 of IPC, and he was arrested on 19.08.2023.
Later, he was granted bail by the Principal Sessions Judge, Chennai on 08.09.2023 in Crl.M.P No.22445 of 2023.

Thereafter, his service was terminated by the Government vide G.O (Ms) No.45,
Cooperation, Food and Consumer Protection (H1) Department, dated 28.02.2024.
Challenging the same, the present writ petition has been filed.

3.However, the learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that though the petitioner was appointed as a Non-Judicial Member in the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission,
Chennai, the petitioner did not file the writ petition seeking reinstatement of service, but only sought payment of salary from 18.08.2023 to 28.02.2024 on the ground that the criminal case registered against him ended in acquittal.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: This Court, by its order dated 11.12.2025 directed the first respondent to decide whether the petitioner is entitled for salary upto 28.02.2024, and if so, to disburse the same to the petitioner and file a report before this Court on or before 18.12.2025.
However, the same was rejected by the impugned compliance report dated 17.12.2025, on the ground of no work, no pay.
The concept of no work, no pay is not applicable to a Non-Judicial Member.
It is only applicable under the labour laws, and treating the petitioner's claim on par with labour laws is not sustainable.
Accordingly, he prayed for appropriate orders.

6.The facts of the present case are not in dispute.

It is an admitted fact that the petitioner was appointed as Non-Judicial Member in the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission,
Chennai, with effect from 15.03.2022 and he assumed charge on 18.03.2022.

Whileso, on the basis of a complaint made by the Personal Assistant to the Hon'ble Judge of this Court dated 18.08.2023,
a criminal case was registered against the petitioner on 19.08.2023.
Later, the criminal case ended in acquittal in favour of the petitioner.

However, his service was terminated by the Government,
vide G.O Ms No.45, Cooperation, Food and Consumer Protection (H1) Department, dated 28.02.2024.
Challenging the said impugned order, the present writ petition has been filed.
However, the relief sought for by the petitioner is not for reinstatement, but only for payment of salary from 19.08.2023 to 28.02.2024.

The respondents refused to pay the salary to the petitioner on the ground of no work, no pay.
The concept of no work, no pay is not applicable to a Non- Judicial Member.
Admittedly, the petitioner was acquitted of the charges and therefore, he is is entitled to salary from 19.08.2023 to 28.02.2024.
